steps:
Do it in a scratch folder made for this, <S> below (for example C:\Scratch\packages-test). File > Export Project empties <S>\export.
1. Unzip export-writes-compiler-packages.zip into <S>, so that <S>\export-writes-compiler-packages.twinproj exists. In a Command Prompt: mkdir <S>\export.
2. Open the project in the twinBASIC IDE. Its Export Path is ${SourcePath}\export. Choose File > Export Project.
3. See <S>\export\Packages: it holds the source of the compiler packages the project uses, VB, VBA, VBRUN and AppGlobalClassProject (475 of the 477 files an export of a two-file project wrote). The project file holds none of them.
4. In a Command Prompt, with <IDE> the folder that holds twinBASIC.exe: "<IDE>\bin\twinBASIC_win32.exe" import <S>\repacked.twinproj <S>\export\ --overwrite. It stops with exit code 999 and writes nothing.
5. Control: "<IDE>\bin\twinBASIC_win32.exe" export <S>\export-writes-compiler-packages.twinproj <S>\fromfile\ --overwrite writes 3 files, Settings and the two sources, and an empty Packages folder, because the project file holds no package.
Re-measured on BETA 995 by `ide-test.bat --only export` (steps 2 to 4).
